notes:
SOURCE. Every IPA string and romanization is copied verbatim from the English Wiktionary entry named in sourceUrl. Bulk harvesting used the kaikki.org machine-readable extraction of English Wiktionary (https://kaikki.org/dictionary/Thai/kaikki.org-dictionary-Thai.jsonl, downloaded 2026-09-07), which exposes the same data as sounds[].ipa. Nothing here was transcribed by hand. All 312 sourceUrl pages were confirmed to exist via the MediaWiki API. 15 rows drawn at random across three seeded rounds were re-fetched from the live pages and their IPA and Paiboon matched byte-for-byte, and every one of the 29 multi-reading and recovered rows was re-fetched in full, confirming all 59 IPA strings and all 59 Paiboon strings on the page itself. The RTGS re-harvest of 2026-09-07 read the 'Royal Institute' rows out of the same dump; 42 rows carrying 58 romanization strings, among them all six multi-reading rows whose readings stay distinct under RTGS, were re-fetched from the live pages and matched byte for byte.

TONE NOTATION — READ BEFORE SCORING. Tone is marked with CHAO TONE LETTERS (˥˦˧˨˩) at the end of each syllable, because that is what Wiktionary's {{th-pron}} template emits. Wikipedia's Help:IPA/Thai describes the same five tones with DIACRITICS OVER THE VOWEL instead (māː, ná). The two notations are not interchangeable and nothing here was converted between them. The five tones appear in this file as: mid ˧, low ˨˩, falling ˥˩, high ˦˥, rising ˩˩˦; all five occur. A scorer that expects diacritic tone marking will mark every row wrong. Segmental symbols are all within the Help:IPA/Thai inventory.

IPA CONVENTION. Broad/phonemic transcription. Enclosing slashes stripped. Syllables are separated by '.'. Unreleased final stops use the release-less diacritic (p̚ t̚ k̚) and diphthong offglides the inverted breve below (ua̯, ia̯, ɯa̯).

ROMANIZATION — RTGS, NOT PAIBOON. 'romanization' holds the Royal Thai General System of Transcription, the Royal Institute standard used on Thai road signs, copied verbatim from the 'Royal Institute' row of the same {{th-pron}} table that supplies the IPA. RTGS is what production emits (convex/lib/romanizationPrompt.ts), so it is what this file scores. All 312 rows and all 29 alternative readings had a Royal Institute form, so nothing is missing and no row carries a not-found marker. The Paiboon form that occupied this field until 2026-09-07 is kept in 'romanizationPaiboon', with 'romanizationPaiboonAlternatives' index-aligned to 'romanizationAlternatives'. Paiboon is REFERENCE ONLY. Never rename it to romanizationAcademic, romanizationStressed or romanizationSandhi: acceptedRomanizations() in scripts/eval-rom.ts reads those three as equally correct answers, and under RTGS a Paiboon answer is wrong, so accepting it would let a wrong engine score 100%.

WHAT RTGS DISCARDS — READ BEFORE SCORING. RTGS is the 26 unmodified Latin letters and nothing else: no tone marks, no accents, no macrons, no doubled long vowels, no ɔ or ɛ. Every value here matches /^[a-z -]+$/, and a diacritic appearing in one is a harvesting bug rather than a variant. It records neither tone nor vowel length, so เขา, ขาว and ข้าว are all 'khao'. That collapse is the standard's own documented limitation and it costs the file discriminating power: 22 of the 28 multi-reading rows have every reading land on ONE identical RTGS string (เขา kǎo/káo both 'khao'), and the 209 word rows carry 208 distinct Paiboon forms but only 185 distinct RTGS forms. Tone and length are still recorded, in 'ipa' and in 'romanizationPaiboon'. An engine that reproduces them is producing Paiboon, and this file does not credit it for that.

SYLLABLE HYPHENS. Wiktionary prints a hyphen at every syllable boundary inside a word — สวัสดี as 'sa-wat-di' — and 130 rows carry at least one. The published standard hyphenates only to break a real ambiguity, before a syllable that starts with a vowel and before 'ng' when the previous syllable ends in a vowel, and joins the rest ('sawatdi'). The source's hyphens are kept because a de-hyphenated string could no longer be re-checked against the page, and because on the phrase rows they are the only syllable boundaries there are: several sentence rows print as one unbroken chain ('khwam-pha-ya-yam-yu-thi-nai'), so stripping the hyphens would assert a word segmentation that no source states. This costs nothing on the headline scores. scripts/eval/lib/romanizationScoring.ts folds a hyphen to a space and also scores a fully joined comparison, taking the better of the two, so an engine answering 'sawatdi' scores 1.0 against 'sa-wat-di'. It does suppress the 'exact' column, which compares the normalized strings literally. Read 'rom' and 'base' for Thai; 'exact' there measures the separator convention, not the engine.

WORD TIER (209 items). Ranked by corpus frequency, not by hand: the Thai Textbook Corpus (ttc_freq) first, then the Thai National Corpus (tnc_freq), both as shipped by PyThaiNLP (https://github.com/PyThaiNLP/pythainlp/blob/dev/pythainlp/corpus/). The top 180 frequency-ranked words surviving the filters below were kept, plus 29 further rows recovered from the same ranking down to rank 1300 (see MULTIPLE READINGS). Wiktionary's Appendix:Thai_Swadesh_list was used as a coverage cross-check.

MULTIPLE READINGS. 28 rows carry more than one attested pronunciation: 27 with two readings and one (สระ) with three. The extra readings live in 'ipaAlternatives', 'romanizationAlternatives' and 'romanizationPaiboonAlternatives', all three positionally aligned — index 0 of one pairs with index 0 of the others — and all three exclude the reading already in 'ipa'/'romanization'/'romanizationPaiboon'. An RTGS alternative that is identical to its row's 'romanization' is kept rather than deduplicated, because dropping it would break that alignment; 22 of the 29 alternatives are such duplicates. The reading placed in 'ipa' is the one Wiktionary lists first, which is normally the everyday sense (เขา → kǎo 'he/she/they', not káo 'horn').

  How the IPA-to-Paiboon pairing was established. Wiktionary emits the Paiboon rows and the IPA rows as two ordered blocks, so the Nth Paiboon belongs with the Nth IPA. That assumption was not taken on trust: it was checked mechanically over the whole dump by converting each Paiboon tone diacritic (none/grave/circumflex/acute/caron) to the Chao contour it implies and comparing it syllable by syllable with the IPA. 18,202 pairs agree and NONE disagree, so the alignment in this file is verified, not assumed. Vowel length is carried in the Paiboon as usual by doubling (kâao vs kâo). The Royal Institute rows form a third block of the same shape, and the 2026-09-07 re-harvest paired them the same way: within an entry the Nth Royal Institute row belongs with the Nth Paiboon row. The two blocks were the same length in every one of the 312 entries, and every gold Paiboon string resolved to exactly one Royal Institute string, with no entry offering two.

  What does NOT count as an alternative reading. Wiktionary pages often carry a second 'pronunciation' that is not a reading of the ordinary word: a province initialism under a pos='name' entry (นม read nɔɔ-mɔɔ is the abbreviation of นครราชสีมา; จบ read jɔɔ-bɔɔ is จันทบุรี), a consonant letter name under pos='character', or a combining/prefix form marked by a trailing '.' in the IPA and '-' in the Paiboon. All three were excluded by provenance, because feeding them to a scorer that credits the closest matching reading would let a wrong transcription score as correct. นม is the clearest case: it was reported earlier as a dropped homograph, but once provenance is applied it has exactly one lexical reading (nom˧ 'milk'), so it is present here as an ordinary single-reading row.

SENTENCE TIER (103 items) — THE SUPPLY IS EXHAUSTED AT THIS SIZE. Wiktionary has NO IPA on usage examples: its example sentences carry a romanization but no transcription, so running prose with an attributable transcription does not exist there. The tier is therefore drawn from Wiktionary headword entries whose part of speech is 'phrase', 'proverb', 'intj' or 'prep_phrase' — phrasebook expressions and full-clause proverbs, each carrying a complete IPA string generated over the whole expression. Exactly 117 such entries of three syllables or more had both an unambiguous pronunciation and a Paiboon romanization; 14 were dropped for cause (see exclusions below) and the remaining 103 are all here. 103 is where the attributable supply stopped, not a target that was hit. Reaching 100 meant accepting two compromises worth knowing about: (a) not every row is a full clause — multi-syllable set expressions and interjections (สวัสดี, ขอบพระคุณ, ราตรีสวัสดิ์) are included, which still test segmentation because Thai is written unspaced and a 3-syllable string with unwritten vowels is exactly where espeak-ng failed; (b) the tail includes ceremonial, archaic and rare-register items (ศุภมัสดุ, ถวายพระพร, สมฤดี) that a learner would not meet. Both are still correct gold — they are just not everyday Thai. If you want an everyday-only subset, cut to the ~60 shortest-gloss rows.

WHAT WAS EXCLUDED AND WHY. (1) Homographs are NO LONGER dropped. Every word with more than one attested lexical reading now carries all of them (see MULTIPLE READINGS), so critical learner vocabulary is present rather than filtered out for being hard — ก็, เขา, ฉัน, หนึ่ง, ท่าน, เจ้า, ไหม, ข้าว, ค่ะ, ผิว, ภรรยา and สระ among them. Earlier revisions of this file excluded them. (2) Combining/prefix forms: Wiktionary lists compound-only readings with a trailing '.' in the IPA and a trailing '-' in the Paiboon (คุณ 'kun-ná-', น้ำ 'nám-'); these were discarded and the free-standing reading kept — they are not alternative readings of the free word. (3) Two rows were rejected as source defects, not curated out for taste: ลูกไม้หล่นไม่ไกลต้น, whose template output reads 'kajl˧' / 'gail' with a coda /l/ that Thai phonotactics does not permit (ไกล is /klaj/), and พูดไปก็ไลฟ์บอย, whose 'lajf˦˥' has a final /f/ for the English loan 'life'. (4) Obsolete/archaic entries, alternative forms, initialisms and abbreviations. (5) Vulgar and slang phrases (ไอ้สัตว์กูขำ and its two spelling variants, ไปโดนตัวไหนมา, วางถุงกาวลงก่อน, อมก, วัดเสมียน), the joke entry 'เจริญ porn', and the numeral LOL entries 555 / ๕๕๕. (6) Spacing-variant duplicates, and 3 of the 5 mechanical 'X-sám-gam-sát' proverb variants. (7) Anything not written in pure Thai script (word tier).

REJECTED SOURCE. The OpenSubtitles-derived Thai frequency list (hermitdave/FrequencyWords) is unusable and was not used: it tokenizes on whitespace, which Thai does not use between words, so its top entries are mojibake fragments (เธ, เน) and untranslated English. Thai Wiktionary (th.wiktionary.org) was not mined either — mixing a second site's transcription conventions into one file would break the internal consistency the scorer depends on.
